candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items); this item tests interdisciplinary collaboration, referral, and coordination of complex rehabilitation needs.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Coordination of multidisciplinary rehabilitation for complex traumatic injury
candidate.educational_objective: Coordinate spinal cord injury rehabilitation through early, individualized multidisciplinary assessment of physical, cognitive, and psychological needs with specialist spinal-injury input when indicated.

options.A: Complete an individualized multidisciplinary assessment that addresses physical, cognitive, and psychological needs and obtains specialist spinal-injury input as indicated
options.B: Limit rehabilitation assessment to mobility because psychological and cognitive needs are outside rehabilitation planning
options.C: Use a single-discipline assessment for every client because complex traumatic injury does not require coordinated expertise
options.D: Delay rehabilitation planning until all long-term functional outcomes can be predicted with certainty

candidate.rationale: A is correct. NICE guideline NG211 recommends that a multidisciplinary team complete a personalized, holistic rehabilitation-needs assessment after traumatic injury that includes physical, cognitive, and psychological functioning. The guideline specifically directs specialist assessment and ongoing specialist spinal cord injury input for people with spinal cord injury. B and C omit domains and expertise explicitly included in the guideline. D is incorrect because rehabilitation assessment and referral should begin early; NICE also cautions that long-term prognosis can be difficult to predict and should not be used as a reason to postpone rehabilitation planning.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current NICE guidance directly supports multidisciplinary, individualized assessment across physical, cognitive, and psychological domains and specialist spinal-cord-injury involvement during rehabilitation.
candidate.source_locator: NICE NG211 → Recommendation 1.2.1: multidisciplinary team should complete a personalized holistic rehabilitation-needs assessment including physical, cognitive, and psychological functioning. Recommendation 1.2.2: specialist assessments for spinal injuries. Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.2: ensure specialist spinal cord injury center contact/referral and seek outreach advice throughout inpatient stay and discharge. Recommendation 1.2.10: long-term prognosis may be difficult to predict and should be discussed after multidisciplinary review.
candidate.source_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
candidate.source_version_date: NICE guideline NG211 published 2022-01-18; current guidance accessed 2026-08-18
